title: Bittern appliance configuration
description: Schema version 3 of appliance.yaml, the single source of truth for a Bittern appliance. Secrets are never stored in this document; camera credentials are referenced from /etc/bittern/secrets.yaml.

schema_version.description: Document schema version. Version 3 is current; version 1 and version 2 documents migrate to version 3 before validation.

cameras.description: Camera inventory. May be empty on first boot.

ipv4Cidr.description: IPv4 address with a prefix length, for example 10.77.0.1/24.

identity.description: Stable device identity. Secrets and generated keys are not part of this section.

timezone.description: IANA time zone name used for logs and schedules.

network.description: The two fixed interface roles from ADR 0005.

lan0.description: House LAN interface. DHCP with a static reservation.

mode.description: lan0 always uses DHCP in schema version 1.

subnet.description: LAN subnet as a network address, for example 192.168.1.0/24.

gateway.description: Expected LAN gateway. DHCP supplies it at runtime; this value lets the validator check it before apply.

match.description: Optional physical NIC match. When absent, lan0 is also the kernel interface name.

cam0.description: Isolated camera interface with no default gateway and IPv6 disabled.

mode.description: cam0 always uses a static address in schema version 1.

address.description: Appliance address on the camera segment, for example 10.77.0.1/24.

match.description: Optional physical NIC match. When absent, cam0 is also the kernel interface name.

cam0Dhcp.description: DHCP and NTP options served only on cam0.

pool_start.description: First address of the dynamic DHCP pool.

pool_end.description: Last address of the dynamic DHCP pool.

reservation_start.description: First address reserved for camera reservations.

reservation_end.description: Last address reserved for camera reservations.

gateway.description: Gateway option advertised to cameras. Usually the cam0 appliance address.

ntp_server.description: NTP server option advertised to cameras. Usually the cam0 appliance address.

camera.description: One camera. Credentials are referenced by key, never included. Optional profiles name the ONVIF media profiles for the main and sub streams.

id.description: Stable camera identifier used in generated configuration.

name.description: Display name shown in the UI.

address.description: Camera address on the cam0 subnet.

rtsp_path.description: RTSP path beginning with a slash.

mac.description: Camera MAC address. When set, Bittern owns a dnsmasq dhcp-host reservation for this camera and its address may sit inside the dynamic pool.

vendor.description: Device-reported manufacturer from ONVIF discovery, for display only.

model.description: Device-reported model or name from ONVIF discovery, for display only.

credentials_ref.description: Key in /etc/bittern/secrets.yaml for this camera's credentials. No credential value belongs here.

profiles.description: Optional ONVIF media profiles for the main and sub streams. An absent profiles object means the camera-level rtsp_path is the only stream. An absent sub means the main stream is the only stream. In both cases both stream names resolve to that one path.

storage.description: Storage roles. Version 3 has a local recording pool and no network storage.

recording.description: Recording pool from ADR 0018. An empty drives list means no recording drive is configured.

mount_point.description: Single media path for the recording pool, normally /var/lib/bittern/media.

drives.description: Pool members. Each entry names exactly one drive by by_id, serial, or device_role. An empty list means no recording drive is configured.

retention_days.description: Days of recordings kept before pruning.

free_space_reserve_gb.description: Free space kept on the recording pool in GiB.

updates.description: Release channel. Update mechanism and update-check policy remain open questions.

channel.description: Release channel recorded by this device.

privacy.description: Privacy-relevant configuration that is already decided. Telemetry and update-check defaults remain open.

tailscale.description: Optional outbound-only remote access from ADR 0009.

enabled.description: Whether Tailscale remote access is enabled.

camera_subnet_route.description: Whether the opt-in 10.77.0.0/24 subnet route is advertised to the tailnet.

linkMatch.description: Physical NIC selector. Exactly one of mac or pci is required; absent match means the logical interface name is the kernel interface name.

mac.description: MAC address of the physical NIC, for example aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:01.

pci.description: PCI address of the physical NIC, for example 0000:01:00.0.

driveSelector.description: One recording pool member. Exactly one selector is required.

by_id.description: Stable /dev/disk/by-id path of the member drive.

serial.description: Serial number of the member drive.

device_role.description: Device role resolved to a member of the recording pool.

hardware.description: Hardware acceleration choices. These are optional and are filled from detection when confident.

device.description: Detector device, such as usb or a device path.

videoDecode.description: Video decode acceleration selected for Frigate.

cameraProfile.description: One ONVIF media profile selected for a camera stream. It stores paths only, never a host, userinfo, credential or full URI.

profile_token.description: Opaque ONVIF profile token from GetProfiles.

rtsp_path.description: RTSP path and query for this profile, beginning with a slash.

snapshot_path.description: Optional ONVIF snapshot path and query for this profile.

width.description: Width in pixels reported by the camera. Empty when the camera does not report it.

height.description: Height in pixels reported by the camera. Empty when the camera does not report it.

codec.description: Codec name reported by the camera, such as h264. Empty when the camera does not report it.

cameraProfilePath.description: A path beginning with a slash, with any query string. It must not contain a scheme separator or userinfo.
